newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen volatile during debate week.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen volatile during debate week.

text.p: Thai stocks will swing sharply this week as a censure debate aimed at toppling Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa takes centre stage, analysts said on Monday.

"It should be real drama, real theatre," said Barry Yates, head of research at the Multi-Credit Corp of Thailand, "Everyone will be watching the developments on television, and we will see that reflected on trading screens."
The opposition has accused Banharn of incompetence and economic mismanagement, among other things, in the no-confidence motion due to be debated in parliament beginning on Wednesday.
The premier's critics have urged him to step down ahead of the debate, but Banharn has vowed to defend himself.

The Thai stock index has been near three-year-lows since last week, depressed by the forced selling by brokerages of stocks held by investors unable to top up margin loan calls, and rumours that some securities firms may be in financial trouble.

However, the market has been firm the last four consecutive days, aided by the presence of part of a 15.7 billion baht (US$628 million) support fund, run by bankers and brokers, to shore up the market, brokers said.
News that the government had launched a 10 billion-baht fund to give loans to investors hit by forced selling of their stocks had also aided sentiment, they said.

But the Government Savings Bank, which had been appointed to run the new fund, said on Monday that loans to cash-strapped investors would only be extended from September 30, and not today as had been expected.
Analysts said the market would react positively to any sign during the debate that Banharn may be unseated.
Yates said he expected trading to reflect patterns seen during a similar debate in May, when some of Banharn's cabinet ministers came under opposition attack in parliament.
Stocks rose in May when the government was vehemently attacked, but fell when it beame clear that Banharn's government would still remain in place.

While local investors could gain from short-term, speculative, profit-making opportunities by playing off developments during the debate, analysts expect major foreign funds to either be sidelined or to sell.

"Politics will be crucial this week," said Union Securities research director Mike Stead, "Given the uncertainty, I see foreigners staying clear or selling as they were in the first four days of last week."
Kerry Securities said the presence of part of the banker/broker support fund had produced an opportunity for fund managers to sell into any technical rally.
"There are a number of European funds in the market that are overweight in Thailand and they are looking for an opportunity to offload," said a Kerry analyst.
Banharn's allies in his 14-month-old coalition have generally promised to support Banharn during the confidence vote, although some vocal party leaders have said otherwise.
Speculation is also rife that Banharn may dissolve parliament ahead of the debate to avoid facing the motion, or win the debate and then quit. He has not commented on this talk.
